content.text: {"tldr":["It reads well at the call site and costs nothing at runtime, so teams keep adopting this pattern.","Callers fill a struct literal, so arguments read by name and any omitted field defaults to zero.","It gives C clearer call sites without new language features or any runtime cost."],"consensus":{"verdict":"mixed","pros":["Call sites read clearly and the pattern costs nothing at runtime.","Compound literals already cover most named-argument needs."],"cons":["Defaults other than zero are not possible.","Adding a struct field changes the size every caller passes.","Mistakes in the macros give unreadable compiler errors."]}}
